'''Nai-Chang Yeh''' ({{lang-zh|t=葉乃裳}}; born 1961) is a Taiwanese physicist specializing in experimental [[condensed matter physics]]. She is a chair professor at [[National Taiwan Normal University]].

== Early life and education ==
She was born and raised in Chiayi, [[Taiwan]]. She graduated from [[National Taiwan University]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]] (B.S.) in 1983, then pursued doctoral studies in the United States. She earned her [[Ph.D.]] in physics from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in 1988.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://yehgroup.caltech.edu/portfolio/nai-chang-yeh/|title=Nai-Chang Yeh|date=2016-01-21|newspaper=Yeh Group|language=en-US|access-date=2017-02-03}}</ref>

In a personal statement on her life and career, Yeh has described her childhood intellectual and artistic curiosity leading her to excel academically. She credits her mother, a mathematics professor, and her Ph.D. supervisor Professor [[Mildred Dresselhaus]] as role models who helped to give her confidence in her ability to succeed in physics.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Yeh|first=Nai-Chang|date=2010|title=A Journey of No Return and No Regrets|journal=The Kaohsiung Journal of Medical Sciences|language=en|volume=26|issue=6S|pages=S17–S21|doi=10.1016/S1607-551X(10)70053-X|pmid=20538242 |issn=2410-8650|doi-access=free|pmc=11922118}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
Her research emphasis is the fundamental physical properties of strongly correlated electronic systems. She is best known for her work on a variety of [[superconductors]], [[magnetic materials]], and superconductor/ferromagnet heterostructures. She is also interested in the physics and applications of low-dimensional electronic systems such as graphene and carbon nanotubes. She contributed to the development of a faster technique to produce high-quality graphene.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Than|first=Ker|date=2015-03-18|title=Caltech Scientists Develop Cool Process to Make Better Graphene|url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/caltech-scientists-develop-cool-process-make-better-graphene-45961|access-date=2021-03-18|website=California Institute of Technology|language=en}}</ref> Her experimental techniques include development of various cryogenic scanning probe microscopes for applications to nano-science and technology, as well as superconducting resonator technologies that have been applied to high-resolution studies of [[superfluid]] phase transitions and [[Bose–Einstein condensation]] in helium gas. She also works on exploring properties of topological insulators.<ref>{{Cite web|last=marciab20|title=Yeh Group publication and video describes new work in 3-D topological Insulators|url=https://iqim.caltech.edu/2016/01/05/yeh-group-publication-and-video-describes-new-work-in-3-d-topological-insulators/|access-date=2021-03-18|website=IQIM|language=en-US}}</ref>

She is Professor of [[Physics]] and the [[Fletcher Jones (American entrepreneur)|Fletcher Jones]] Foundation Co-Director of the Kavli Nanoscience Institute at the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nai-Chang Yeh {{!}} www.pma.caltech.edu|url=https://pma.caltech.edu/people/nai-chang-yeh|access-date=2017-02-03|website=pma.caltech.edu|language=en}}</ref> Yeh was the first female professor in that department when she joined in 1989.<ref name=":0" /> She is also part of the Caltech Institute for Quantum Information and Matter.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nai-Chang Yeh|url=https://iqim.caltech.edu/profile/nai-chang-yeh/|access-date=2021-03-18|website=IQIM|language=en-US}}</ref> She is currently a Chair Professor at [[National Taiwan Normal University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=University Chair Professor |url=https://www2.phy.ntnu.edu.tw/index.php/en/university-chair-professor-en/ |access-date=2024-07-04 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
She has been recognized by a number of professional associations:

*Fellow, [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]; 
*Fellow, [[American Physical Society]]; 
*Fellow and Chartered Physicist, The [[Institute of Physics]], UK; 
*David and Lucile Packard Fellow for Science and Engineering;<ref>{{Cite web|title=Yeh, Nai-Chang|url=https://www.packard.org/what-we-fund/science/packard-fellowships-for-science-and-engineering/fellowship-directory/yeh-nai-chang/|access-date=2021-03-18|website=The David and Lucile Packard Foundation|language=en-US}}</ref>
*[[Sloan Research Fellow]];
*Academician, [[Academia Sinica]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academia Sinica - Press Releases {{!}} 2024 Academicians and Honorary Academicians Announced |url=https://www.sinica.edu.tw/en/News_Content/55/2640 |access-date=2024-07-04 |website=www.sinica.edu.tw |language=en-US}}</ref>

She was lauded in ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine on November 18, 1991, as a scientific "rising star" in California.<ref>''Time Magazine'' "Galaxy of Stars" in Special Issue on California, Vol. 138 #20, P.73, Nov 18, 1991.</ref>
She is cited in the [[American Men and Women of Science]].
